name: Event coincidence analysis (ECA)
title: Do leveraged-fund unwinds come right before settlement-fail spikes?
what: Counts how often extreme weeks in one series fall just after extreme weeks in another, with direction, lag and a null.
pick_line: Conditional ECA: does unwind → fails survive once equity-vol and repo-spread spike weeks are conditioned out?
data: Public aggregates (NY Fed fails, OFR repo, CFTC TFF, SEC Form PF); descriptive only
one: A quarter of fails spikes follow a big leveraged-fund unwind a week earlier; builds show nothing.

picture.la: Usual tool: cross-correlation (weak r = −0.16 at lag 1)
picture.lb: ECA: unwinds precede fails spikes; builds don't

findings.h: Fails spikes follow big leveraged-fund unwinds by one week.
findings.t: Of 39 financing-fails spike weeks (top 10% of weekly log change, 2018-05 to 2025-12), 26% come exactly one week after a big unwind week (bottom 10% change in leveraged-fund net short, UST 2Y+5Y+10Y futures). Random placement gives about 10% (circular-shift p = 0.008). Same or previous week: 38% vs 18%, Holm p = 0.0096 over 48 pre-registered tests.
findings.note: Big build weeks: 10% one week before (p = 0.54), no different from chance. Reverse direction (unwind one week after a fails spike): 15%, p = 0.16.

findings.h: It holds in both halves and at other thresholds.
findings.t: The same/previous-week precursor rate beats its null 95th percentile in 2018-05..2022-06 (42% vs 37%) and 2022-07..2025-12 (35% vs 30%), and at 80% (55% vs 44%) and 95% (25% vs 20%) event thresholds: all five pre-registered checks pass.
findings.note: The trigger-rate version fails in the second half (39% vs 39%). The coincident weeks include 2020-03-04, -11 and -18 and 2025-02-19, 2025-03-05 and 2025-09-24.

findings.h: The textbook Poisson test is too generous on these clustered series.
findings.t: On 2,000 circularly shifted (independent by construction) pairs, CoinCalc's Poisson test rejects at 5% in 9.2% (fails ← spread) and 9.4% (DVP ← fails) of cases. Overall, 15 of 48 tests have Poisson p < 0.05; only 10 pass the circular-shift null and 3 survive Holm.
findings.note: Below our pre-set 'miscalibrated' flag of 10%, but nearly double the nominal 5%. That motivates the Math avenue.

findings.h: Monthly Form PF borrowing spikes do not line up with fails.
findings.t: Form PF tab 8.27 prime-broker and total borrowing growth (top 20% months, 2013-05..2025-12, 152 months) shows no coincidence with fails-spike months at lags 0, 3 or 6 months, in either direction (smallest p = 0.24; all Holm p = 1).
findings.note: Consistent with the 11-14 CRQA (prime-broker growth: no link). Low power: with 3-month windows and 31 events, the null 95th percentile is already about 0.6.
